source_resources.title: GitHub Actions Documentation
source_resources.author: GitHub, Inc.
source_resources.permission_basis: GitHub product documentation published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; the curriculum links to it and paraphrases concepts without importing text.
source_resources.prerequisites: YAML familiarity, shell commands, and Git hosting vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary reference for pipeline stages, required status checks, and branch protection mechanics that the local CI practice runner mirrors in a disposable environment.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Public documentation site; exact workflow syntax evolves with the product.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Pipeline stage semantics (lint, test, package, deploy gate) are exercised offline by scripts/ci_practice_runner.py; no GitHub account or push authorization is required for the practice.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Equivalent pipeline concepts under a different provider; GitHub Actions matches the hosted-workflow conventions used in this project's delivery story.
Self-hosted CI server documentation; GitHub Actions better matches the hosted pipeline model the learner will meet first.

source_resources.title: Site Reliability Engineering, Chapter 8: Release Engineering
source_resources.author: Dinah McNutt (ed. Betsy Beyer, Tim Harvey), in Site Reliability Engineering (eds. Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Jennifer Petoff, Niall Richard Murphy; Google)
source_resources.permission_basis: Google hosts a free-to-read web edition; the curriculum links to it without importing text.
source_resources.prerequisites: Build and deployment vocabulary; version control basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely used industry reference for hermetic builds, release approval gates, and rollback-ready deployment doctrine that anchor Day 81's controlled delivery and verified rollback exercises.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Free web edition hosted by Google; the print edition is paid.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The controlled delivery and rollback runbook is fully executable offline via the scripts/ci_practice_runner.py deploy stage, which emits recorded evidence payloads.

compared_candidates.license: Copyright Martin Fowler; free public web article
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Focused single-pattern bliki on blue/green cutover; the SRE chapter covers the wider release-engineering lifecycle including build hermeticity and rollback policy.
Foundational paid text on deployment pipelines; the SRE web edition provides equivalent operational doctrine at zero cost with a stable public URL.

source_resources.title: Pro Git, Second Edition
source_resources.author: Scott Chacon and Ben Straub
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 3 (Git Branching), Section 7.7 (Reset Demystified), Sections 5.2/6.2 (Contributing to a Project)
source_resources.permission_basis: Linking only; no book text reproduced in curriculum content; reuse limited to noncommercial references consistent with CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic git status/log/diff vocabulary from earlier study days
source_resources.selection_rationale: Freely licensed reference for branching, merging, conflict resolution, and safe recovery vocabulary used through the delivery workflow.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Readable free at git-scm.com; availability depends on the site staying online.
source_resources.safe_fallback: git help <command> and the Git manual pages ship with Git and cover the same commands offline; every required workflow is stated locally in the lesson.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Interactive but requires a GitHub account and an external service; disposable local repositories keep the exercise self-contained.
Vendor-owned prose with no permissive license; Pro Git covers the same ground under CC BY-NC-SA.

source_resources.title: Continuous Integration
source_resources.author: Martin Fowler
license_restrictions: Article is linked, not copied; pipeline practice uses the repository's own runner
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external linking to a freely accessible web article; no text is imported into curriculum materials.
source_resources.prerequisites: Version control basics, automated test suites, and build vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standard practitioner reference defining the CI contract this block rehearses: every change merges to a mainline verified by an automated build and test run, and failures are fixed before further work proceeds.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publicly hosted on martinfowler.com; long-term availability not guaranteed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The CI gate contract (lint, test, package, verdict) is executed locally by scripts/ci_practice_runner.py with no external dependency.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Provider-specific workflow syntax; Fowler's article states the vendor-neutral CI discipline the learner must internalize first, while the docs are kept as the pipeline-mechanics source.
Vendor-oriented tutorial; Fowler's original definition keeps the explanation tool-agnostic and historically important.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Practices of Continuous Integration: Make the Build Self-Testing; Fix Broken Builds Immediately
